# stdx.endpoint

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

HTTP bindings of operations (FRAMEWORK_DESIGN.md §14): an endpoint is a
route whose handler is an `app.Operation`.

    endpoint.bind({
        method: #post,
        path: "/orders",
        operation: create,
        input: fn(_params: {}, body: NewOrder) { body },
        status: 201,
    })

The path parameters decode into the input function's first parameter
(a record naming the pattern's `:name`s) and the body into its second;
malformed input is a 400 reply naming the input path, before the
operation runs. Each request is a new `app.Call` (its correlation is the
request's `x-correlation-id` when it has one, echoed in the reply). The
operation's output is encoded with its schema; its expected errors are
answered as their type says (`@derive(HttpError)` with `@http.status`,
`@http.code`, and `@http.codes` on the error enum), a server error
without its details.
The route's name is the operation's id and its summary the operation's
documentation, so URLs and OpenAPI come from the same registration.

## Types

### `Context`

```badger
pub type Context = {
```

An endpoint's transport policies: who the caller is (`identify` gives
the verified actor, `none` for an anonymous request, or a failure to
answer), how long a request may take from its arrival (so time waiting
for admission counts), which gate admits it, and the largest body it
accepts (in bytes; the request is already buffered, so this bounds what
is decoded, not what was read).

### `Failure`

```badger
pub type Failure = { status: Int, code: Symbol, message: String }
```

How a refused request is answered (an `identify` that refuses it): a
status, a stable code, and a message for the client.

## Functions

### `bearer`

```badger
fn bearer(verify: fn(String) -> Option<app.Actor>) -> fn(http.Request) -> Result<Option<app.Actor>, Failure>
```

Identity from `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`: `verify` gives the token's
actor. A request without the header is anonymous (a policy decides
whether that is allowed); a malformed header or a token `verify`
refuses is a 401.

### `bind`

```badger
fn bind<P, B, I, O, E, Eff>(binding: { method: Symbol, path: String, operation: app.Operation<I, O, E, Eff>, input: fn(P, B) -> I, status: Int, }) -> route.Route where P: Codec, B: Codec, O: Codec, E: HttpStatus, E: Display
```

Bind an operation to a method and path (see the module documentation),
with `public()` policies.

### `bind_in`

```badger
fn bind_in<P, B, I, O, E, Eff>(context: Context, binding: { method: Symbol, path: String, operation: app.Operation<I, O, E, Eff>, input: fn(P, B) -> I, status: Int, }) -> route.Route where P: Codec, B: Codec, O: Codec, E: HttpStatus, E: Display
```

Bind an operation under `context`'s policies. A request is checked in
order: body size (413), identity (the failure `identify` gives), path
parameters and body (400), admission (503 when the gate's queue is
full or the deadline passes while waiting), and then the operation
runs with the verified actor and the deadline in its call. A `#get` or
`#delete` endpoint has no body, and an empty body is `{}`: the input
function's second parameter decodes from it. The operation's error is
answered as its type says (`HttpStatus`: `derive(HttpError)` reads each
variant's `@http.status` and `@http.code`): a client error with its
code and message, a server error with its status only.

### `call_of`

```badger
fn call_of(request: http.Request) -> app.Call !{Io}
```

The call a request makes: a new root call, joined to the caller's
correlation when the request carries `x-correlation-id`.

### `failure`

```badger
fn failure(status: Int, code: Symbol, message: String) -> Failure
```

### `health`

```badger
fn health(h: app.Health) -> List<route.Route>
```

Health routes: `GET /health/live` answers 200 while the process serves
at all; `GET /health/ready` answers the health report, 200 when the
application accepts work and 503 otherwise (starting, stopping, or a
required check failing).

### `public`

```badger
fn public() -> Context
```

No identity, deadline, or gate; bodies up to 1 MiB.
